analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. Darkbloom.swift:32 exposes the new Addon CLI. StatusCommand.swift:118 calls StatusCommand+AddonHold.swift:7-11 to display the first hold and additional-hold count; nil/empty snapshots produce no line. This is diagnostic output, not a serving-authorization decision. The existing daemon-health stale-snapshot warning and coordinator-bound authorization display remain unchanged. No supplied change modifies encryption, keys, cache scoping/storage, attestation, billing or privileged fan authority, and no concrete regression is established in this scope.
AddonCommandTests.swift:11-31 exercise command parsing, 30–600-second lease bounds, default non-force release, and rejection of missing/stale/noncurrent daemon identity or absent add-on support. Lines 34-67 cover hold/lock diagnostics and snapshot serialization. These tests express contracts but do not establish runtime enforcement.
Integration must examine the newly exposed Addon command and hold service implementations, not supplied here: caller authority and process binding, lease/lock recovery (including expired holds retained while a lock is held), force-release semantics, and inference drain/admission during hold transitions. These interactions matter to availability and TB-003/TB-007, and must preserve the independent TB-011/T-052/T-053 authorization boundary. Also verify Addon.describe's handling of externally supplied labels before terminal output. Missing implementations are coverage limits, not evidence of vulnerabilities; the local changes alone do not establish a threat-model update requirement.
